advice: Propose a scratch-lifetime change confined to the n=512 wrapper: replace the full512 kernel’s per-64-row-band 128 KiB stack reservation with one 128 KiB reservation before the eight-band loop. Keep the current packing cursor, scratch offsets, traversal, K loops, FP32 FMOPA order, and stores unchanged. At each band, reset SP and x3 to the reserved scratch base before packing; after packing, restore SP to that base before compute; restore the saved stack top before smstop. This differs from the measured reserve-scratch-once source only if it changes the mechanism or generated code; the supplied history already records that exact reservation and reset scheme as `libxsmm-full512-reserve-scratch-once`, which was not promoted. Therefore do not submit that alias as a new experiment. No distinct legal scratch-lifetime improvement is established by the supplied evidence; abstain unless the swarm board specifies a genuinely different source change.
risks: The prior reserve-once experiment is already measured and failed the repeated promotion gate; repeating it under another name would not be useful. Any new variant must retain the fixed ABI, FP32 arithmetic, thread count, tolerance, general-size behavior, timed allocation/packing, complete license notices, and non-reentrant safety. If a distinct ranked change is later supplied, check scratch bounds for both row halves, full output overwrite, fresh-input correctness at n=512, general sizes and tails, n<=0, and allocation-failure fallback; then use ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with best-of-three timing, the unchanged adoption gate, and held-out check.
